# loading libraries
```{r}
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
```


# Load the data
```{r}
df <- read_excel("jdk.xlsx", sheet = "Sheet1")

# Fix the Student_ID column (rows 51-600 contain formulas like "=1+A51")
# We'll just create a clean sequential ID
df$Student_ID <- 1:nrow(df)

# Convert categorical variables to factors
df$Gender <- as.factor(df$Gender)
df$Major <- as.factor(df$Major)
df$Passed_Class <- as.factor(df$Passed_Class)

# Check structure
str(df)
cat("Number of rows:", nrow(df), "\n")



```

# Question 1: Histogram of GPA

```{r q1-histogram, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5}
ggplot(df, aes(x = GPA)) +
  
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.2,
                 fill = "yellowgreen", 
                 color = "blue",
                 alpha = 0.55) +
  
  geom_vline(
    aes(xintercept = mean(GPA)), 
    color = "red",
             linetype = "dashed", 
    linewidth = 1) +
  
  labs(title = "Histogram of GPA",
       subtitle = paste("   Red dashed line = Mean GPA =", 
                        round(mean(df$GPA), 4)),
       x = "GPA", y = "Frequency") +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15)
```

```{r}
gpa_summary <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c("N", "Mean", "Median", "Std. Dev.", "Min", "Max", "Skewness"),
  Value = c(
    nrow(df),
    round(mean(df$GPA), 4),
    round(median(df$GPA), 4),
    round(sd(df$GPA), 4),
    round(min(df$GPA), 4),
    round(max(df$GPA), 4),
    round(mean((df$GPA - mean(df$GPA))^3) / sd(df$GPA)^3, 4)
  )
)

kable(gpa_summary,
      caption = "Table 1: Descriptive Statistics for GPA",
      col.names = c("Statistic", "Value"),
      align = c("l", "r")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE,
                position = "center")
```


# Report:QUIZ 1                                                           *** Shape: - 
-Approximately normal / roughly symmetric (skewness ≈ 0.04, very close to 0). Slight bimodal tendency due to the repeating data pattern.                ***Approximate center: Mean ≈ 3.21, Median ≈ 3.20




# Question 2: Bar Chart of Major

```{r q2-bar, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5}
ggplot(df, aes(x = Major, fill = Major)) +
  geom_bar() +
  geom_text(stat = "count", aes(label = after_stat(count)),
            vjust = -0.5, size = 4) +
  labs(title = "Count of Students by Major",
       x = "Major", y = "Frequency") +

```






```{r q2-table}
major_tbl <- as.data.frame(table(df$Major))
colnames(major_tbl) <- c("Major", "Frequency")
```

# Question 3: Boxplot of Study_Hours by Gender

```{r q3-boxplot, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5}
ggplot(df, aes(x = Gender, y = Study_Hours, fill = Gender)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.75, outlier.color = "red",
               outlier.shape = 16, outlier.size = 2) +
  labs(title = "Boxplot of Study Hours by Gender",
       x = "Gender", y = "Study Hours") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```


```{r q3-table}
gender_summary <- df %>%
  group_by(Gender) %>%
  summarise(
    N        = n(),
    Median   = median(Study_Hours),
    Q1       = quantile(Study_Hours, 0.25),
    Q3       = quantile(Study_Hours, 0.75),
    IQR      = IQR(Study_Hours),
    Min      = min(Study_Hours),
    Max      = max(Study_Hours),
    Outliers = sum(Study_Hours < quantile(Study_Hours, 0.25) - 1.5 * IQR(Study_Hours) |
                   Study_Hours > quantile(Study_Hours, 0.75) + 1.5 * IQR(Study_Hours))
  )

kable(gender_summary,
      caption = "Table 3: Study Hours Summary by Gender",
      col.names = c("Gender", "N", "Median", "Q1", "Q3", "IQR",
                    "Min", "Max", "Outliers"),
      align = c("l", rep("r", 8))) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE,
                position = "center")
```


# Report:Q3                                                              
- Median Study Hours: Female = 14, Male = 15, Non-binary = 14               - Outliers: Using the 1.5×IQR rule, no outliers are detected in any gender group.





# Question 4: Scatter Plot — Study_Hours vs GPA

```{r q4-scatter, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5}
ggplot(df, aes(x = Study_Hours, y = GPA)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Scatter Plot: Study Hours vs GPA",
       subtitle = paste("Pearson r =", round(cor(df$Study_Hours, df$GPA), 3)),
       x = "Study Hours", y = "GPA") +
  theme_minimal()
```



```{r q4-table}
model <- lm(GPA ~ Study_Hours, data = df)

cor_tbl <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Pearson correlation (r)", "R-squared",
             "Intercept", "Slope (Study_Hours)", "p-value (slope)"),
  Value = c(
    round(cor(df$Study_Hours, df$GPA), 4),
    round(summary(model)$r.squared, 4),
    round(coef(model)[1], 4),
    round(coef(model)[2], 4),
    format(summary(model)$coefficients[2, 4], scientific = TRUE)
  )
)

kable(cor_tbl,
      caption = "Table 4: Correlation and Regression Results (GPA ~ Study_Hours)",
      col.names = c("Metric", "Value"),
      align = c("l", "r")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE,
                position = "center")
```


### Report:Q4
- Direction: Positive — as Study_Hours increases, GPA increases.     - Strength: Very strong positive relationship (r ≈ 0.931, R² ≈ 0.867). - Trendline: GPA = 1.852 + 0.086 × Study_Hours. Each additional study hour is associated with a 0.086-point increase in GPA.





## PART 2: HYPOTHESIS TESTING

### Question 5: One-Sample T-Test — GPA vs 3.0

```{r q5-ttest}
t_test_gpa <- t.test(df$GPA, mu = 3.0, alternative = "two.sided")
print(t_test_gpa)
```




```{r q5-table}
q5_tbl <- data.frame(
  Item = c("Null Hypothesis (H0)", "Alternative Hypothesis (H1)",
           "Sample Mean", "t-statistic", "Degrees of Freedom",
           "p-value", "95% CI Lower", "95% CI Upper",
           "Decision (alpha = 0.05)"),
  Value = c("mu = 3.0", "mu != 3.0",
            round(mean(df$GPA), 4),
            round(t_test_gpa$statistic, 4),
            t_test_gpa$parameter,
            format(t_test_gpa$p.value, scientific = TRUE),
            round(t_test_gpa$conf.int[1], 4),
            round(t_test_gpa$conf.int[2], 4),
            "Reject H0")
)

kable(q5_tbl,
      caption = "Table 5: One-Sample T-Test Results (GPA vs 3.0)",
      col.names = c("Item", "Value"),
      align = c("l", "r")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE,
                position = "center") %>%
  row_spec(9, bold = TRUE, background = "#d4edda")
```



###Report:                                                                    ***H₀: μ = 3.0 — The mean GPA is equal to 3.0.                                ***H₁: μ ≠ 3.0 — The mean GPA is significantly different from 3.0.        ***Sample mean: 3.2099 | t-statistic: 10.939 | p-value: < 0.0001    ***Conclusion: Since p < 0.05, we reject H₀. The mean GPA is significantly higher than 3.0.




## Question 6: Two-Sample T-Test — Study_Hours by Gender (Male vs Female)

```{r q6-ttest}
df_gender <- df %>% 
  filter(Gender %in% c("Male", "Female"))
t_test_gender <- t.test(Study_Hours ~ Gender, data = df_gender,
                        alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = FALSE)
print(t_test_gender)
```


```{r q6-table}
q6_means <- df_gender %>%
  group_by(Gender) %>%
  summarise(N = n(),
            Mean = round(mean(Study_Hours), 4),
            SD   = round(sd(Study_Hours), 4))

kable(q6_means,
      caption = "Table 6a: Group Statistics for Study Hours by Gender",
      col.names = c("Gender", "N", "Mean Study Hours", "Std. Dev."),
      align = c("l", "r", "r", "r")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "center")

q6_tbl <- data.frame(
  Item = c("Null Hypothesis (H0)", "Alternative Hypothesis (H1)",
           "t-statistic", "Degrees of Freedom", "p-value",
           "95% CI Lower", "95% CI Upper", "Decision (alpha = 0.05)"),
  Value = c("mu_Male = mu_Female", "mu_Male != mu_Female",
            round(t_test_gender$statistic, 4),
            round(t_test_gender$parameter, 2),
            round(t_test_gender$p.value, 4),
            round(t_test_gender$conf.int[1], 4),
            round(t_test_gender$conf.int[2], 4),
            "Fail to Reject H0")
)

kable(q6_tbl,
      caption = "Table 6b: Independent Two-Sample T-Test Results",
      col.names = c("Item", "Value"),
      align = c("l", "r")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "center") %>%
  row_spec(8, bold = TRUE, background = "#fff0cd")
```



##Report:                                                                  
- H₀: μ_Male = μ_Female (no difference in mean study hours)                - H₁: μ_Male ≠ μ_Female (significant difference exists)                  - Group means: Female = 14.087, Male = 13.913                      - t-statistic: 0.4611 | p-value: 0.6449                            - Conclusion: Since p = 0.6449 > 0.05, we fail to reject H₀. There is not enough evidence at the 5% level to conclude a significant difference. (Note: marginally non-significant — would be significant at α = 0.10.)






## Question 7: Paired T-Test — Pre_Test_Score vs Post_Test_Score
```{r q7-ttest}
t_test_paired <- t.test(df$Post_Test_Score, df$Pre_Test_Score,
                        paired = TRUE, alternative = "two.sided")
print(t_test_paired)
```



```{r q7-table}
diff_scores <- df$Post_Test_Score - df$Pre_Test_Score

q7_means <- data.frame(
  Test = c("Pre_Test_Score", "Post_Test_Score", "Difference (Post - Pre)"),
  Mean = c(round(mean(df$Pre_Test_Score), 4),
           round(mean(df$Post_Test_Score), 4),
           round(mean(diff_scores), 4)),
  SD = c(round(sd(df$Pre_Test_Score), 4),
         round(sd(df$Post_Test_Score), 4),
         round(sd(diff_scores), 4))
)

kable(q7_means,
      caption = "Table 7a: Paired Test Score Summary",
      col.names = c("Test", "Mean", "Std. Dev."),
      align = c("l", "r", "r")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "center")

q7_tbl <- data.frame(
  Item = c("Null Hypothesis (H0)", "Alternative Hypothesis (H1)",
           "Mean Difference", "t-statistic", "Degrees of Freedom",
           "p-value", "95% CI Lower", "95% CI Upper",
           "Decision (alpha = 0.05)"),
  Value = c("mu_diff = 0", "mu_diff != 0",
            round(mean(diff_scores), 4),
            round(t_test_paired$statistic, 4),
            t_test_paired$parameter,
            format(t_test_paired$p.value, scientific = TRUE),
            round(t_test_paired$conf.int[1], 4),
            round(t_test_paired$conf.int[2], 4),
            "Reject H0")
)

kable(q7_tbl,
      caption = "Table 7b: Paired T-Test Results",
      col.names = c("Item", "Value"),
      align = c("l", "r")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "center") %>%
  row_spec(9, bold = TRUE, background = "#d4edda")
```



### Report:   
- H₀: μ_diff = 0 (no significant difference between Pre and Post scores)   - H₁: μ_diff ≠ 0 (significant difference — scores improved)              - Mean Difference: +8.64 points                                  - t-statistic: 90.4102 | p-value: < 0.0001                          - Conclusion: Since p < 0.05, we reject H₀. Test scores improved significantly from Pre to Post (+8.64 points on average).




## Question 8: Chi-Square Test of Independence — Major vs Passed_Class

```{r q8-chisq}
contingency_table <- table(df$Major, df$Passed_Class)
chi_test <- chisq.test(contingency_table)
print(chi_test)
print(round(chi_test$expected, 2))
```

```{r q8-table}
# Observed contingency table
obs_tbl <- as.data.frame.matrix(contingency_table)
obs_tbl <- cbind(Major = rownames(obs_tbl), obs_tbl)
rownames(obs_tbl) <- NULL

kable(obs_tbl,
      caption = "Table 8a: Observed Contingency Table (Major x Passed_Class)",
      col.names = c("Major", "No", "Yes"),
      align = c("l", "r", "r")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "center")

# Expected contingency table
exp_tbl <- as.data.frame.matrix(round(chi_test$expected, 2))
exp_tbl <- cbind(Major = rownames(exp_tbl), exp_tbl)
rownames(exp_tbl) <- NULL

kable(exp_tbl,
      caption = "Table 8b: Expected Contingency Table",
      col.names = c("Major", "No", "Yes"),
      align = c("l", "r", "r")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "center")

# Cramer's V
cramers_v <- sqrt(as.numeric(chi_test$statistic) /
                  (sum(contingency_table) * (min(dim(contingency_table)) - 1)))

q8_tbl <- data.frame(
  Item = c("Null Hypothesis (H0)", "Alternative Hypothesis (H1)",
           "Chi-square statistic", "Degrees of Freedom", "p-value",
           "Cramer's V", "Decision (alpha = 0.05)"),
  Value = c("Major and Passed_Class are independent",
            "Major and Passed_Class are associated",
            round(as.numeric(chi_test$statistic), 4),
            as.numeric(chi_test$parameter),
            format(chi_test$p.value, scientific = TRUE),
            round(cramers_v, 4),
            "Reject H0")
)

kable(q8_tbl,
      caption = "Table 8c: Chi-Square Test Results",
      col.names = c("Item", "Value"),
      align = c("l", "r")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "center") %>%
  row_spec(7, bold = TRUE, background = "#d4edda")
```


### Report:

- H₀: Major and Passed_Class are independent (no association)

- H₁: Major and Passed_Class are associated (dependent)

- Chi-square statistic: χ² = 1155.5556 | df: 2 | p-value: < 0.0001

- Cramer's V: 0.5092 (moderate-to-strong association)

- Conclusion: Since p < 0.05, we reject H₀. There is a significant association between Major and Passed_Class. Only Business students failed (26.7%), while all STEM and Humanities students passed.





### Summary Table of All Hypothesis Tests

```{r summary-table}
summary_tbl <- data.frame(
  Question = c("Q5", "Q6", "Q7", "Q8"),
  Comparison = c("GPA vs 3.0",
                 "Study Hours: Male vs Female",
                 "Pre vs Post Test Score",
                 "Major vs Passed_Class"),
  Test = c("One-sample t-test",
           "Two-sample t-test (Welch)",
           "Paired t-test",
           "Chi-square test"),
  Statistic  = c(
    paste0("t = ", round(as.numeric(t_test_gpa$statistic), 4)),
    paste0("t = ", round(as.numeric(t_test_gender$statistic), 4)),
    paste0("t = ", round(as.numeric(t_test_paired$statistic), 4)),
    paste0("chi-sq = ", round(as.numeric(chi_test$statistic), 4))
  ),
  df = c(
    as.numeric(t_test_gpa$parameter),
    round(as.numeric(t_test_gender$parameter), 2),
    as.numeric(t_test_paired$parameter),
    as.numeric(chi_test$parameter)
  ),
  p_value = c(
    format(t_test_gpa$p.value, scientific = TRUE),
    round(t_test_gender$p.value, 4),
    format(t_test_paired$p.value, scientific = TRUE),
    format(chi_test$p.value, scientific = TRUE)
  ),
  Decision = c(
    ifelse(t_test_gpa$p.value < 0.05, "Reject H0", "Fail to Reject H0"),
    ifelse(t_test_gender$p.value < 0.05, "Reject H0", "Fail to Reject H0"),
    ifelse(t_test_paired$p.value < 0.05, "Reject H0", "Fail to Reject H0"),
    ifelse(chi_test$p.value < 0.05, "Reject H0", "Fail to Reject H0")
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Color rows based on decision
row_colors <- ifelse(summary_tbl$Decision == "Reject H0", "#d4edda", "#fff3cd")

kable(summary_tbl,
      caption = "Table 9: Summary of All Hypothesis Tests (alpha = 0.05) — Auto-Populated",
      col.names = c("Question", "Comparison", "Test", "Statistic",
                    "df", "p-value", "Decision"),
      align = c("c", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "l")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, position = "center") %>%
  row_spec(1, background = row_colors[1]) %>%
  row_spec(2, background = row_colors[2]) %>%
  row_spec(3, background = row_colors[3]) %>%
  row_spec(4, background = row_colors[4])
```
